#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
#
# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
# fine with it.
#
# Env:
#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).
#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-marker}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"

case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
  marker) ;;
  pc)
    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
      exit 77
    fi
    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
    ENTER_PC=$(printf '%s\n' "$NM_OUT" | awk '$3=="_hybrid_enter_pc"{print $1}')
    EXIT_PC=$(printf '%s\n' "$NM_OUT"  | awk '$3=="_hybrid_exit_pc"{print $1}')
    if [ -z "${ENTER_PC:-}" ] || [ -z "${EXIT_PC:-}" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE pc]: missing _hybrid_enter_pc/_hybrid_exit_pc symbols"
      exit 1
    fi
    ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use marker|pc)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# 128 MB matches the QEMU virt machine default; vsim uses the same size.
SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 2/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?
set -e

# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu). The
# run ends here -- the cycle figure is the vsim mcycle delta -- so anything
# other than a clean drain is a hard failure.
if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim expected exit 200 (drain), got $VSIM_RC"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

# Opt-in: mcycle/minstret must strictly increase from QEMU 1's drain
# to vsim's drain. Offsets locked by state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624,
# minstret@632).
if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ] && [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ]; then
  read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
  echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
  echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
  if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)"

# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
# fine with it.
#
# Env:
#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).
#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via
#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
#                   relies on this; ./andesim run always passes them explicitly.
#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
#   CHECK_PRIV=<0|1|3>         assert both drained state files carry this
#                              privilege (L6: 0=U, 1=S, 3=M).
#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.
#   QEMU_CPU        -cpu argument for both QEMU legs (default
#                   andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512, pairing the default vsim
#                   engine). Override together with VSIM_BIN to run a
#                   fixture on another engine, e.g. the S/U-capable
#                   ax66_makatau for the rt_priv_* fixtures (the default
#                   ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only).

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-marker}"
QEMU_CPU="${QEMU_CPU:-andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"

case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
  marker) ;;
  pc)
    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
      exit 77

    # $VSIM_ELF). ./andesim run always passes them explicitly. When a caller
    # leaves BOTH unset (e.g. the bulk runner scripts/run_e2e.sh), derive them
    # from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via objdump, so pc mode needs no
    # per-fixture config and no planted boundary symbols. A partial set or a
    # derivation miss falls through to roi_resolve_pair's required-vars error.
    if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] && [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"

         && MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")"); then
        ROI_START="0x${MARKERS%% *}"
        ROI_END="0x${MARKERS##* }"
        export ROI_START ROI_END

    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1

VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")

VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()

  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)

  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \

  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \

  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
  exit 1

  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \

# scripts/run_e2e.sh.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)

    | awk '

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
#
# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
# fine with it.
#
# This is the single-fixture form: one FIXTURE, QEMU 1 -> vsim, print the
# kernel_cycles figure. Marker mode only; the pc-mode resolver and the
# parallel bulk runner (scripts/run_e2e.sh) come next.
#
# Env:
#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker (default). pc mode arrives with the roi resolver.
#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF  override built paths.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-marker}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
  marker) ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (marker only in this slice)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# 128 MB program RAM matches the QEMU virt machine default; vsim uses the
# same size so the shared mmap survives the QEMU 1 -> vsim handoff.
SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"

echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 2/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 </dev/null >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1

# Anything else is a hard failure: the cycle figure is only valid when vsim
# drained cleanly.

  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
# is the measured region's cycle count.
read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
if [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] && [ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/e2e.sh must print kernel_cycles -- the vsim mcycle delta over the
# measured region (vsim drain - QEMU1 drain, offset 624) -- for both
# trigger modes (marker, pc), so the `./andesim run --mode hybrid
# --trigger marker|pc` surface carries the cycle figure.
#
# Fixture: rt_c_v_matmul.elf (marked RVV GEMM). Marker mode uses the
# ROI marker HINTs in the source; PC mode resolves the boundaries
# from the binary itself (no planted _hybrid_*_pc labels).
#
# Manual TDD smoke test (runs real QEMU+vsim round-trips); not wired into
# scripts/run_e2e.sh.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)
FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul

. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/log.sh"
. "$ROOT/setup.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# Resolve the PC immediately after `jal vmatmul_kernel` in the marked
# GEMM ELF; that's the PC at which vsim drains for PC mode (ROI_END).
# Recompiling the fixture relocates this address, so we derive it from
# objdump every run.
resolve_post_jal_pc() {
  local elf="$1"
  "$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump" -d "$elf" \
    | awk '
        /jal[[:space:]]+.*<vmatmul_kernel>/ { matched = 1; next }
        matched { sub(":", "", $1); printf "0x%s\n", $1; exit }
      '
}

check_mode() {
  local mode="$1"; shift
  local out rc n
  out=$(env FIXTURE="$FIXTURE" TRIGGER_MODE="$mode" EXPECT_RC=0 TIMEOUT=120 \
        "$@" bash "$ROOT/tests/e2e.sh" 2>&1)
  rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 77 ]; then
    echo "[skip] $mode round-trip skipped (rc=77, e.g. toolchain missing)"
    return 0
  fi
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$out"; fail "$mode round-trip did not exit 0 (rc=$rc)"; }
  n=$(echo "$out" | sed -nE 's/.*kernel_cycles\][[:space:]]*([0-9]+).*/\1/p' | head -1)
  { [ -n "$n" ] && [ "$n" -gt 0 ]; } \
    || { echo "$out"; fail "$mode: kernel_cycles not a positive integer (got '${n:-}')"; }
  echo "[ok] $mode round-trip printed kernel_cycles=$n"
}

check_mode marker

if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ]; then
  echo "[skip] pc round-trip: HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN unset (run \`source ./setup.sh\`)"
else
  POST_JAL_PC=$(resolve_post_jal_pc "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/$FIXTURE.elf")
  [ -n "$POST_JAL_PC" ] || fail "could not resolve post-jal PC for vmatmul_kernel"
  check_mode pc ROI_START=vmatmul_kernel ROI_END="$POST_JAL_PC"
fi

echo "PASS test_kernel_cycles"
